vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: bear-share-sync
Version: 1.0.1

The skill bundle is a legitimate utility for syncing Bear notes tagged '#share' to a JSON Canvas and sending previews via BlueBubbles. It uses the 'grizzly' CLI to interact with Bear and 'jq' for safe JSON manipulation in 'scripts/sync_share_notes.sh'. While the script handles sensitive data (Bear API tokens and note content), its operations are transparent, follow the stated purpose, and lack indicators of malicious intent, exfiltration to unauthorized endpoints, or command injection.

llm.summary: Review before installing because this skill can read Bear notes through a local token, persist note excerpts, stage or send them via BlueBubbles, and includes a ClawHub publishing step.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md purpose is coherent for a share-sync pipeline, but it is broader and higher-impact than the short registry description: it combines Bear note extraction, persistent canvas updates, messaging, and ClawHub publishing.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The documented workflow includes external messaging and publishing without an explicit confirmation, diff review, or visibility warning before note-derived content leaves the local Bear/canvas workflow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec and no automatic installer, but the included shell script relies on external tools and services such as grizzly, jq, BlueBubbles/OpenClaw messaging, and clawhub that are not declared as registry requirements.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill uses a local Bear token file, reads note content, writes a persistent canvas/state file, and may stage message previews in /tmp; these are sensitive but only partially represented by the metadata.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Processed note IDs and note-derived canvas nodes persist across runs, and the broader pipeline can use authenticated messaging/publishing accounts without a clearly defined retention, review, or rollback boundary.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Only install if you intend Bear notes tagged #share to be extracted into an agent canvas and potentially messaged or published. Run with DRY_RUN first, inspect generated canvas changes, set BlueBubbles targets carefully, remove temporary preview files, and do not run the ClawHub publish step until you have reviewed exactly what will be uploaded.

evidence.explanation: The skill makes an authenticated ClawHub publish operation part of the share-sync pipeline after note-derived canvas updates, but does not require a content review, diff, or explicit confirmation before publishing.
evidence.snippet: Automated pipeline: Bear #share  JSON Canvas  BlueBubbles preview  ClawHub publish. ... clawhub publish ./bear-share-sync --slug bear-share-sync --name "Bear Share Sync" --version <semver>

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Keep publishing as a separate manual step, require explicit user confirmation and a reviewed diff, and clearly declare the publishing capability and required account authority.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: A full pipeline run could publish skill changes or note-derived files under the user's ClawHub account, potentially exposing shared-note content or changing what other users install.

evidence.explanation: The script stages a Bear note excerpt and the messaging target in fixed /tmp files for the BlueBubbles/OpenClaw send path, which creates unclear local access and cleanup boundaries.
evidence.snippet: preview=" New shared note: $title\n\n$(echo "$body" | head -c 500)" ... echo "$BLUEBUBBLES_TARGET" > /tmp/bear_share_last_target ... echo "$preview" > /tmp/bear_share_last_preview

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Use secure temporary files with restrictive permissions, delete them after use, validate the destination, and require a final user confirmation before sending previews.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: A note preview and phone number or chat GUID may remain on disk and could be read by other local processes or sent to the wrong destination if the target is misconfigured.

evidence.explanation: The script uses a local Bear/grizzly token file to read Bear notes. This is expected for the stated Bear sync purpose, but it is sensitive local account/app access.

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Use the least-privileged Bear/grizzly token available, avoid tagging sensitive notes with #share, and declare this credential requirement in metadata.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: Installing or running the skill gives the workflow access to Bear notes tagged #share through the configured token.

evidence.explanation: The skill persists Bear note titles and excerpts into a canvas that may be reused as agent context or knowledge.
evidence.snippet: node_json=$(jq -n ... '{id: $id, type: "text", text: " \($title)\n\($summary)", x: 0, y: 0, width: 280, height: 120, color: "4"}') ... jq --argjson node "$node_json" '.nodes += [$node]' "$CANVAS_FILE"

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Review notes before tagging them #share, treat canvas text as untrusted data rather than instructions, and define retention or deletion rules for generated nodes.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: Content in #share notes can become long-lived agent knowledge and could influence later agent behavior if note text contains instructions or misleading information.

evidence.explanation: The workflow depends on external local CLIs and authenticated services whose versions, provenance, and permissions are outside the supplied install spec.
evidence.snippet:
- Bear app running with `grizzly` CLI installed and token configured
- `jq` available on PATH
- (Optional) BlueBubbles channel configured for preview delivery
- (Optional) `clawhub` CLI authenticated for publishing

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Declare required binaries and optional services in metadata, pin or document trusted installation sources, and verify each tool before running the pipeline.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: The safety of the workflow also depends on the installed grizzly, jq, BlueBubbles/OpenClaw, and clawhub tooling on the user's machine.

abnormal_behavior_control.summary: The main concern is the documented ClawHub publishing step without an explicit review or confirmation gate; external tool provenance is also a note.

permission_boundary.summary: The skill uses a local Bear/grizzly token and may rely on authenticated messaging or ClawHub accounts; this is purpose-aligned but sensitive.

sensitive_data_protection.summary: Bear note excerpts are persisted into a canvas and, when messaging is configured, staged in fixed /tmp files and potentially sent via BlueBubbles.
